claims.text: Minor boron additions to HfMoNbTaTiZr promote formation of boride precipitates at grain boundaries.
The boron-induced precipitates have a hexagonal close-packed structure.
Intergranular boride precipitates enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion improves high-temperature mechanical and thermoelastic performance relative to boron-free HfMoNbTaTiZr.
The baseline processed HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy has a homogeneous microstructure without significant intergranular precipitates.
Intergranular boride-precipitate density is expected to increase with boron content.
Boron-induced intergranular precipitates reduce crack initiation during high-temperature deformation.
Boron-induced intergranular precipitates alter dislocation activation at grain boundaries during high-temperature deformation.
Changes in grain-boundary cohesion and dislocation activation govern the alloy's strength, ductility, and thermoelastic response.
Boron-doped samples should exhibit greater ductility than the boron-free baseline.
Boron-doped samples should exhibit improved creep resistance relative to the boron-free baseline.
Boron doping should alter high-temperature yield strength and elastic modulus relative to the boron-free baseline.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold under controlled thermomechanical processing and testing at temperatures up to 1273 K.
The effects are sensitive to alloy composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The initial-state and controlled-comparison descriptions indicate that the baseline receives thermomechanical processing after casting, whereas the baseline field calls it 'as-cast.' These are materially different baseline conditions.
